engine.label: nine passes, in order: intake · still true? · summary · cause and blocked_by · group, by the theme's own rules · priority, by the theme's own list · the three whos (decides first · can do it, the triage owner first · affected) · cross-references and outputs · log every act
engine.plain: A sorting desk for any long list. It reads a theme's list through that theme's adapter, drops what is already fixed, checks every item carries its summary, names each cause and what blocks it, then groups items into actions by the theme's own grouping rules (components by fix, operations by detector and brand). It ranks actions by the theme's own priority list (neither grouping nor priority is built into the engine), says who decides, who can do it (the triage owner first) and who is affected, links each item to related work elsewhere, and logs every act. The engine names no person, path or priority rule: all of that comes from the theme pack.

issues.text: No one owns the engine yet
issues.affects: the whole component: who builds it, who keeps the passes the same across domains
issues.why: Without an owner, each list grows its own copy of these passes, which is the drift this component exists to remove.
issues.fix: Name an owner. The suggestion is the team: she owns the PM tool, the likeliest third domain, and the system-integration engine.
issues.fix_impact: One owner builds the first version and approves domain adapters.
issues.if_ignored: Two lists (component issues and red tests) keep running as one-off scripts.
issues.resolved: the team owns the engine (the team "I own engine", decision log 981094a4a)

issues.text: What the triage owner may do alone is not ruled
issues.affects: the triage owner's lane on every list
issues.next: Decide at the team's meeting today. Ask the owner first: may the team, through Claude, fix spelled-out issues in the owner's components with every change in the decision log and a one-line undo? Yes → Option 3; no → Option 2.
issues.why: Until it is ruled, every item still ends in an owner's yes, which is the bandwidth problem this was meant to solve.
issues.fix: Proposed (for discussion, not ruled): Option 3. A triage owner may apply a ruled default, or a fix the issue's brief already spells out, in an owner's component, with the owner told rather than asked. Four limits: the brief names the change and a test proves it; no test assertion is weakened or removed; nothing changes how a live pipeline behaves (those stay "triage owner drafts, owner lands"); every change is a decision-log record with a one-line undo, and owners see their areas' changes there. The alternatives were Option 1 (owners asked first, as today) and Option 2 (ruled defaults only). Full text with examples: triage/proposals/triage-owner-scope.json.
issues.fix_impact: Decides who does the 297 component issues tagged "after a ruling" (about 197 in the owner's components, 70 in the team's, 18 in the team's, 29 with no owner); the triage owner clears that lane, and owners see what changed in their area in the decision log.
issues.if_ignored: The triage owner keeps asking owners about issues they would agree with anyway.
issues.resolved: Ruled 2026-10-02: option 3. the owner said yes to the first-step question (relayed by the team: "owner decided yes on option 3"). Limits: the summary names the fix and a test proves it; no test check weakened; no live-pipeline change; every change in the decision log with a one-line undo.

issues.text: The definitions mix up an item's cause with what blocks it
issues.affects: definitions file for red tests: 'a card awaiting approval is a ruling'
issues.next: Split cause from blocked_by in the definitions schema
issues.why: The red-test trial mislabelled 4 of 34 suites because of that one line, even though it reached the right action.
issues.fix: Give every item two fields: a cause class (what is wrong) and blocked_by (an unapproved card, a pending decision, or nothing).
issues.fix_impact: Every domain's definitions file changes shape once; the passes don't.
issues.if_ignored: Cards awaiting approval keep being reported as rulings, and the counts mislead.
issues.resolved: cause and blocked_by are two fields (the team "ok", 4b36a7a90); applied to red-tests/DEFINITIONS-red-tests.md pass 2

issues.text: Nothing can close an issue on a component page except that component's next run
issues.affects: 39 component issues already fixed by the README fill, still open
issues.next: Choose the write-back path for closures
issues.why: Triage finds fixed items but cannot retire them, so the queue carries dead weight until each component happens to run again.
issues.fix: Either let the next system run read triage's closure proposals, or let the team mark an issue closed with its evidence.
issues.fix_impact: Fixed items leave the queue within a week instead of whenever a run comes.
issues.if_ignored: The 39 stay open, and every report shows them again.
issues.resolved: the team may mark an issue closed with its evidence: SCHEMA §5a, decision log 981094a4a; render.py f25c4dac3, crosscheck.py 0a414be2d

issues.text: Where triage's records live is not decided
issues.affects: its runs and the decisions people make on its asks
issues.why: Decisions need to be findable later (who said yes to what) without becoming a second voting system beside review.
issues.fix: Add two kinds, triage-runs and triage-decisions, with written_by: triage; reuse review's record shape.
issues.fix_impact: Two new kind files and the review shape borrowed.
issues.if_ignored: Decisions stay in chat and handoff notes and can't be counted.
issues.resolved: one `triage` record kind, runs under runs/triage/<list>/<date>/ (the team "ok", 4b36a7a90); kind file live in ATL-28 (triage record kind), 9c1367b81

issues.affects: the P0 tier on the component-issue dry run: 101 items
issues.next: Atlas actions are now weighted by issue tier (P0 8 · P1 4 · P2 2 · P3 1), but issue tiers still come from the dry run's keyword rules; moves into atlas.json with the refactor (#11).
issues.why: In a sample of 7 P0s, 2 were false. A wrong P0 spends the triage owner's first hour on the wrong thing.
issues.fix: Read severity from the brief the run writes (SCHEMA §5 severity) and use keywords only when it is missing.
issues.fix_impact: P0 becomes a judgement made by whoever read the code.
issues.if_ignored: The queue keeps opening with false alarms.

issues.affects: the largest run so far: 685 items, about 7 agents and roughly 0.5–1 million tokens (inferred)
issues.why: A weekly tick over several lists has to fit the slots and a budget.
issues.fix: Measure one full weekly run per domain before turning on the tick; cap tokens per run.
issues.fix_impact: The tick runs inside the slot budget, or it waits.
issues.if_ignored: Cost surprises once three or four lists run weekly.

issues.text: Customer service may not need an adapter at all
issues.affects: tickets live in the helpdesk, outside the workspace
issues.next: Set aside this round: two themes only (components / atlas, operations).
issues.why: Helpdesks like Zendesk, Gorgias and Intercom already triage with AI; pulling tickets in may duplicate that.
issues.fix: Check the helpdesk's own triage first; feed its themes into the weekly asks rather than copying tickets in.
issues.fix_impact: Either no adapter, or a thin one that reads themes.
issues.if_ignored: An adapter built for a job the helpdesk already does.

issues.text: The red-test reporter sometimes shows the wrong failing line
issues.affects: the reporter's first_failing_line on 2 of 34 suites: a passing docstring, and a line that didn't reproduce
issues.why: The red-test adapter reads that line first, so a wrong line sends the first look the wrong way.
issues.fix: Have the reporter record the first failing assertion, not the first line starting with FAIL.
issues.fix_impact: One change in the reporter; every red-test reader benefits.
issues.resolved: reporter records the first failing assertion: TI-22 (first failing assertion), merged 80d5854a5

issues.text: The decision log's five proposed acts and the reopen rule are not carded
issues.affects: the decision log every theme writes, and every close
issues.next: Carded and dispatched as ATL-32 (triage change trail), a3b9ac629. No triage-owner change lands in an owner's component until it merges.
issues.why: A close with no reopen rule can't be undone through the record.
issues.fix: Extend the kind from ATL-28 (triage record kind) and add the reopen sentence.
issues.fix_impact: Every act is on the record and reversible.
issues.if_ignored: Acts live only in pages and commits.
issues.resolved: ATL-32 (triage change trail) merged 2026-10-02: change, draft, sign, undo and decide acts with required-when rules; SCHEMA §5a undo reopens. Writer: components/triage/tools/file_record.py (7 tests).

issues.text: 60 of 83 component actions were created without a summary
issues.affects: the components queue: the actions the team works
issues.next: Derive the 60 from their issues' summaries once ATL-31 (remaining issue briefs) lands, the way operations does; from now on no action is created without one.
issues.why: The rule since 2026-10-02 is that anything triage creates is born with its eight parts; these predate it.
issues.fix: Build each action's eight parts from its issues' summaries (why, who, evidence, fix, what changes, if ignored, lane, priority across them), as tools/metrics_insights.py does for operations.
issues.fix_impact: Every action on the components queue explains itself, like operations' do.
issues.if_ignored: the team opens 60 actions with only a headline to go on.
issues.resolved: 2026-10-02: ATL-31 (remaining issue briefs) merged; tools/triage_fill.py built the 60 action summaries from their issues' summaries. 83 of 83 actions carry one.
